newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NUM confident Northam strike will go ahead.
newsitem.headline: NUM confident Northam strike will go ahead.

text.p: South Africa's powerful National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Wednesday it was confident that a strike at Northam Platinum Ltd would go ahead.
NUM regional coordinator Mahlakeng Mahlakeng told Reuters the result of a strike ballot among Northam's more than 3,000 union members would be known on Wednesday afternoon.

"We started counting this morning and we anticipate (that) we should have a concrete answer as to the percentage by 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) this afternoon. We believe we will get the majority," Mahlakeng said.
Northam owners, Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, said on Monday it had reached deadlock with the union over wages and that the company was bracing itself for a strike.
The mine, which produced 75,365 ounces of precious metals in concentrates in the three months to September, has some 5,500 workers -- 3,300 of whom are members of NUM.
The remaining workers have already acccepted a 10 percent wage increase and Mahlakeng said although the union had initially demanded a 15 percent pay hike, it was prepared to accept 10 percent.
"The actual focal point is the parity," he said, adding that Northam's minimum wage of around 556 rand was well below that of other mines.
"The strike is going to go ahead unless management revises its position," he added.
Northam recorded a net loss before capital spending of 7.39 million rand in the September quarter after turning in a profit of 8.17 million in the previous quarter.
Analysts said the mine would be hard pressed to deal with a strike by almost 66 percent of its workforce.

Violent ethnic conflict at the mine in August had already seen 660 Zulu workers leave the mine, although they have since been replaced. The Zulus were all in key posts operating machines or mine hoists.
